slides.title: Ristretto, normale, lungo: what changes?
slides.subtitle: Only the water changes, and so does the taste.

slides.title: The word is the recipe
slides.body: Ristretto is Italian for restricted. Lungo means long. Normale is the standard shot between them. The word tells you how much water goes through the coffee.
slides.highlight: Length is the water. Size is the coffee.

slides.myth: A ristretto is just an espresso stopped early.
slides.truth: Cutting a normal shot short tastes sour. A true ristretto uses the same coffee with about half the water, planned from the start.

slides.title: Why the cup changes
slides.body: Water keeps pulling more out of the coffee the longer it runs. The early part tastes sweeter. The later part adds the bitter, roasty notes.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: Keep your coffee dose the same and change only the water. Taste each cup side by side, then pick the length you like.

slides.title: Same coffee, less or more water
slides.body: Ristretto is short and sweeter. Lungo is long and more bitter. Normale sits between.
